title: Launch-day vLLM/SGLang + Ollama support becomes open-weight MoE release bar
body: Mistral 3's launch shipped its Large 3 sparse MoE flagship (41B active / 675B total) tuned for vLLM and SGLang while sizing its 14B/8B/3B dense variants for Ollama, llama.cpp, and MLX on release. This mirrors how Qwen 3.5 and DeepSeek's latest sparse checkpoints already land with same-week serving-runtime and local-runtime coverage. As the open-weight frontier consolidates around a handful of MoE families converging on similar sparse-activation designs, coordinated launch-time runtime support stops being a differentiator and becomes the expected minimum. Expect the next major open-weight MoE releases to treat first-party vLLM/SGLang serving paths plus Ollama/llama.cpp/MLX local packaging as a non-negotiable launch deliverable rather than a community follow-up, because Apache 2.0 permissive terms only convert to real commercial adoption when practitioners can deploy the weights the day they drop.

summary: Mistral 3 launched with its MoE flagship tuned for vLLM/SGLang and dense variants packaged for Ollama, llama.cpp, and MLX. As open-weight MoE families converge on shared sparse designs, launch-day runtime support shifts from differentiator to release-quality baseline for the next major releases.
